identity.industry: Oil & Gas Upstream Equipment / Specialty Seamless Pipes

summary.oneLiner: Maharashtra Seamless Limited is a seamless and ERW steel pipe manufacturer serving oil and gas, infrastructure and industrial applications, with steel pipes and tubes accounting for 98.80% of turnover.
summary.business: The Company manufactures seamless and ERW steel pipes and tubes for oil and gas exploration and production, transportation, power, infrastructure and industrial applications. Its customers comprise exploration and production companies, infrastructure contractors, refineries, boiler manufacturers and cylinder manufacturers. Alongside the pipes business it operates wind power and solar power assets, and it is progressively shifting mix towards specialised, value-added products such as cold-drawn pipes, drill pipes, sour-service subsea pipes and premium connections.

currentContext.strengths: Strong balance sheet and substantial treasury position, described by Management as an important competitive advantage in a cyclical industry, enabling working capital and capex to be funded largely through internal resources|Established customer relationships that allowed the Company to sustain dispatch levels through a year of lower order inflows|Technical expertise and a diversified product portfolio spanning cold-drawn pipes, cylinder pipes, drill pipes, sour-service subsea seamless pipes and premium connections, addressing import-substitution and higher-value applications|Licensing arrangement with JFE through Jindal Premium Connections, giving access to advanced premium connection technology|Pricing discipline: the Company chose to protect profitability rather than pursue volumes through aggressive pricing|Multi-location manufacturing footprint across Maharashtra and Telangana plus captive wind and solar power assets
currentContext.strategies: Strengthen the core seamless and specialised pipe business, particularly across the oil and gas and infrastructure sectors.|Increase the contribution of specialised and value-added products (cold-drawn pipes, cylinder pipes, drill pipes, sour-service subsea seamless pipes, premium connections) to improve differentiation and realisations, and reduce dependence on commodity-oriented volumes.|Move from being primarily a volume-driven manufacturer to an increasingly technology- and value-added-product-oriented company, using the licensing arrangement with JFE through Jindal Premium Connections for advanced premium connection technology.|Improve capacity utilisation by removing operational bottlenecks in existing manufacturing infrastructure.|Expand export markets selectively, strengthening presence in the United States and developing new markets and customers across geographies to build a diversified international customer base.|Maintain financial discipline: a strong liquidity position, capital deployed selectively towards projects offering appropriate long-term returns, and a disciplined treasury approach emphasising preservation of capital, liquidity and risk-adjusted returns.|Evaluate selective inorganic opportunities where assets can be acquired at appropriate valuations and the transaction can create long-term shareholder value.|Build a fully integrated ERP-driven organisation connecting manufacturing, procurement, inventory, sales, logistics and finance for better information flow, faster decisions and improved working-capital management.|Sustain cost control and productivity improvement across productivity, energy efficiency, procurement, inventory optimisation and elimination of inefficiencies.|Maintain pricing discipline rather than pursuing volumes through aggressive pricing.|Pursue import substitution as a structural opportunity, supported by the Make in India initiative.|Continue CSR focus on healthcare, education and rural development in communities around operations.
currentContext.expansion: The Company undertakes capital expenditure selectively, favouring projects that enhance manufacturing capabilities, remove operational bottlenecks and improve long-term returns, and funds the programme through internal accruals. The key project completed during FY 2025-26 was the cold-drawn pipes facility. The Company also progressed with the Telangana finishing line project, which is intended primarily to address an existing finishing bottleneck; Management expects it to enable better utilisation of existing production capacity that is currently constrained by the absence of commensurate finishing capacities. No commissioning date is stated for the Telangana finishing line. Alongside physical capex, the Company continued work on new product development and premium connections, with a licensing arrangement with JFE through Jindal Premium Connections giving access to advanced premium connection technology, and is building a fully integrated ERP platform connecting manufacturing, procurement, inventory, sales, logistics and finance. Management states it will continue to evaluate capital expenditure opportunities based on market demand, strategic relevance and expected returns while maintaining a disciplined approach to capital allocation, and will also evaluate selective inorganic opportunities where assets can be acquired at appropriate valuations. Plant-level technology-absorption work during the year covered the 7" Mill, 6" Mill, 14" Mill, OCTG, Coating Plant and the United Seamless Plant, including drive and PLC upgrades, and new sizes rolled at the United Seamless Plant. The Directors' Report also notes that the Board approved on 22 May 2026 a Scheme of Arrangement for demerger of two business undertakings into two subsidiary companies, which is under further review.
currentContext.mdna: Demand for seamless pipes is closely linked to oil and gas exploration and production capex, pipeline infrastructure, energy security, industrial activity and infrastructure development; oil and gas is one of the principal demand drivers.|During FY 2025-26 the pace of expenditure and tendering activity in the oil and gas sector remained below expectations, which affected order inflows and revenue visibility.|Increased availability of competitively priced imports, particularly from China, placed pressure on domestic pricing and realisations and on margins.|Revenue moderation was driven by slower order inflows, lower oil and gas expenditure and pressure on market realisations, while quantity dispatched did not see material change.|Going forward, improved capacity utilisation, higher value addition and a recovery in oil and gas-related demand are expected to remain important drivers of operating performance.|Long-term structural demand support from India's growing energy requirements, oil and gas exploration and production, pipeline networks, city gas distribution, water infrastructure and industrial projects.|Medium and long-term opportunity from import substitution and increasing demand for technically specialised products; ability to develop value-added products, maintain quality and build long-term customer relationships is expected to remain a key differentiator.|Near-term recovery in the seamless pipe business is expected to remain dependent on the revival of oil and gas expenditure, tendering activity and project awards.|Key catalysts named for recovery in volumes, realisations and operating profitability: a sustained improvement in oil and gas expenditure and tendering activity, together with moderation in import pressure.|Margin levers cited: pricing discipline, improved product mix, manufacturing efficiencies and greater contribution from value-added products.|The strong balance sheet and substantial treasury position are described as a competitive advantage in a cyclical industry, providing flexibility to evaluate strategic opportunities when valuations become attractive.|Exports are influenced by global trade developments, competitive pricing and evolving tariff and trade arrangements; realignment of global supply chains is seen as an opportunity for India and for MSL.|Management describes FY 2025-26 as a year of operating moderation rather than financial stress, driven by external and cyclical factors, and remains cautiously optimistic on India's energy and infrastructure structural growth.|The order book was at its lowest towards the initial part of FY 2025-26 and gradually revived as the year progressed but still remained below the levels anticipated.|Order booking declined significantly during the first quarter as tendering activity by oil and gas companies remained below expectations.|The order book subsequently improved and remained at healthy levels through the year, providing reasonable near-term revenue visibility.|The order book generally provides approximately three to four months of revenue visibility.|The ability to replenish the order book during a period of subdued industry demand is cited as evidence of the Company's established market position and customer relationships.

risks.risk: Demand risk — dependence on oil and gas and infrastructure capital expenditure
risks.note: The business is significantly linked to the oil and gas and infrastructure sectors, so a slowdown in government or oil and gas capital expenditure may affect order inflows and capacity utilisation. In FY 2025-26 expenditure and tendering activity by oil and gas companies remained below historically anticipated levels, which directly hit order inflows and revenue visibility. Mitigation: diversify the product portfolio, develop value-added products, expand customer relationships and pursue export opportunities.

risks.risk: Import and competitive risk — dumping of seamless pipes from China
risks.note: Aggressive pricing and increased imports, particularly from China, may adversely affect domestic prices and margins. Continued dumping was described as a significant challenge for the domestic industry, contributing to pressure on product realisations and margins, and the Chairman states such imports can adversely impact domestic manufacturing, employment and future investments. Mitigation: focus on value-added products, import substitution, technical differentiation and customer approvals, while monitoring trade-remedial measures including continuation of anti-dumping duties.

risks.risk: Realisation and pricing risk in a cyclical industry
risks.note: Lower market realisations together with weaker order inflows compressed operating profitability during the year. The Company maintained pricing discipline and did not pursue volumes at the expense of profitability, which itself moderated order intake. Levers cited to protect profitability are pricing discipline, improved product mix, manufacturing efficiencies and greater contribution from value-added products.

The order book was at its lowest towards the initial part of FY 2025-26 and, though it revived, remained below anticipated levels; it generally provides only approximately three to four months of revenue visibility. While tenders remained available, conversion of tenders into actual orders and project execution was slower than anticipated, affecting the revenue trajectory.

risks.risk: Project execution risk on capital expenditure
risks.note: Capital expenditure projects may be affected by execution, commissioning or cost-related risks. Mitigation: projects are monitored through defined execution and review mechanisms with emphasis on cost control and timely implementation. The Telangana finishing line project remained in progress at year end.

Changes in tariffs, trade agreements, geopolitical developments and international demand may affect exports, which contribute 10.67% of total turnover across 4 international countries. The MD cites geopolitical tensions, the conflict involving Iran, crude oil price volatility, shipping and supply-chain disruption and changing trade policies as headwinds. Mitigation: diversify geographical exposure and focus on technically differentiated products and markets.

Steel pipes and tubes account for 98.80% of turnover (NIC code 24311, manufacture of tubes, pipes and hollow profiles), leaving the Company with essentially no diversification away from one activity; customers are concentrated in exploration and production companies, infrastructure contractors, refineries, boiler manufacturers and cylinder manufacturers.

risks.risk: Financial market and liquidity risk overseen by the Risk Management Committee
risks.note: The Directors' Report states business operations are exposed to a variety of financial risks such as market risks (foreign exchange risk, interest rate risk and price risk) and liquidity risk. A Risk Management Committee constituted by the Board implements and monitors the Board-approved Risk Management Policy and identifies risks that in the Board's opinion may threaten the existence of the Company; input-cost exposure is reinforced by the MD's reference to volatile energy, raw-material and logistics costs.

risks.risk: Employee attrition in a specialised-skill manufacturing operation
risks.note: Operations require specialised technical capabilities, yet the BRSR discloses permanent-employee turnover of 19.54% in FY 2025-26 (24.36% in FY 2024-25 and 27.29% in FY 2023-24), against permanent-worker turnover of 7.17%. Continued investment in employee training and development is stated as important to maintaining product quality, safety and productivity.

one-line thesis: Q3FY26 margins improved sequentially due to a one-off inventory markdown reversal rather than structural demand strength, while management reiterated a conservative cash-hoarding stance despite 50% market cap in liquid assets. Growth remains binary on Union Budget oil & gas capex and the delayed launch of premium connections in 6 months.
financial scorecard: Revenue: Not explicitly disclosed (Volumes: 1.01 lakh tons, flat QoQ vs 1.03 lakh tons in Q2); EBITDA/Margin: Improved sequentially (guided INR 10k-15k/ton) driven by inventory markdown reversal; PAT: Boosted significantly by Other Income (gold/silver market sentiment) and tax shields from USL merger; Order Book: INR 1,302 cr (as of Jan 20), 33% Oil & Gas (ONGC/Oil India); Net Debt: Negative (Net Cash ~INR 3,500 cr liquid investments). One-offs: Inventory markdown reversal boosted margins; Other Income volatility from treasury.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Dependent on Union Budget oil & gas capex; Margin: Expected to sustain INR 10,000-15,000/ton; Order Inflow: Steady replenishment despite muted govt spend; Capex/Commissioning: Telangana finishing line partial start in Q4FY26, Premium Connections production in 6 months.
order book & pipeline: INR 1,302 crores (as of Jan 20, 2026); 33% Oil & Gas sector (ONGC, Oil India); Balance industrial/other sectors; Drill pipe orders currently nil but high-margin when present.
segment / subsidiary detail: Seamless pipes (core): Margin improved due to mix and markdown reversal. ERW: Margins up on product mix. Value-added (4/5 categories made): Cold drawn, cylinder, sour service subsea, drill pipes (no current orders). Premium connections: Not yet manufactured, royalty agreement signed, production expected in 6 months.
growth verticals / optionality: Inorganic M&A (distressed assets only); Premium connections market entry (50k-100k tons/year opportunity); Telangana finishing line unlocking 1 lakh ton bottleneck; Potential FTA benefits with Europe (under review).
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA/ton guided at INR 10k-15k. Raw material (HRC) price hikes passed through via back-to-back booking. Safeguard duty on steel not applicable to seamless segment. Margin improvement in Q3 was primarily due to reversal of prior quarter's inventory markdown.
capex / expansion: Total planned INR 852 cr. Active projects: Cold drawn pipes (completed); Telangana finishing line (POs issued INR 90 cr, partial commissioning in Q4FY26). Premium connections capex unspecified but timeline set for 6 months.
capital allocation: Aggressive cash conservation (INR 3,500 cr liquid investments, ~50% of market cap). Dividend quadrupled FY22-FY24, maintained in FY25 despite lower profits. No buyback or special dividend planned; management prioritizes survival/cyclical resilience over short-term distribution. Treasury portfolio returned >24% in 9M FY26.
risks & watch-items: Government capex delay (Oil & Gas dependency); Chinese import dumping (20-25% of domestic market); Demand stagnation without budget stimulus; Execution risk on premium connections launch; CFO turnover history (though current CFO tenure 1.5 years).
management quality / tone: Defensive and conservative; Emphasizes survival track record (35 years) over growth at any cost; Dismissive of shareholder pressure to deploy cash; Transparent on one-offs (markdown reversal) but opaque on specific product mix percentages.
non-obvious takeaways: The margin beat is largely an accounting artifact (inventory markdown reversal) telegraphed last quarter, not operational leverage. The company sits on massive cash (INR 3,500 cr) earning >24% returns, effectively acting as a hedge fund with a pipe manufacturing attached, yet refuses to return excess capital citing industry bankruptcy risks.

| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Import dumping from China and muted government capex delaying volume growth | Jindal Saw Ltd | beneficiary | Med | Competitor in premium connections; MSL entering this segment may intensify competition, but overall sector tailwinds from anti-dumping duties benefit domestic players. |
| High raw material volatility and lack of finishing capacity | Maharashtra Seamless Ltd | beneficiary | High | Telangana finishing line unlocks trapped capacity; strong treasury buffers against cyclical downturns better than peers. |

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures seamless and ERW steel pipes and tubes for oil and gas exploration and production, transportation, power, infrastructure and industrial applications. Its customers comprise exploration and production companies, infrastructure contractors, refineries, boiler manufacturers and cylinder manufacturers. Alongside the pipes business it operates wind power and solar power assets, and it is progressively shifting mix towards specialised, value-added products such as cold-drawn pipes, drill pipes, sour-service subsea pipes and premium connections.

Premium connections: Not yet manufactured, royalty agreement signed, production expected in 6 months.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: INR 1,302 crores (as of Jan 20, 2026); 33% Oil & Gas sector (ONGC, Oil India); Balance industrial/other sectors; Drill pipe orders currently nil but high-margin when present.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: Dependent on Union Budget oil & gas capex; Margin: Expected to sustain INR 10,000-15,000/ton; Order Inflow: Steady replenishment despite muted govt spend; Capex/Commissioning: Telangana finishing line partial start in Q4FY26, Premium Connections production in 6 months.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Inorganic M&A (distressed assets only); Premium connections market entry (50k-100k tons/year opportunity); Telangana finishing line unlocking 1 lakh ton bottleneck; Potential FTA benefits with Europe (under review).

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Demand for seamless pipes is closely linked to oil and gas exploration and production capex, pipeline infrastructure, energy security, industrial activity and infrastructure development; oil and gas is one of the principal demand drivers.
- During FY 2025-26 the pace of expenditure and tendering activity in the oil and gas sector remained below expectations, which affected order inflows and revenue visibility.
- Increased availability of competitively priced imports, particularly from China, placed pressure on domestic pricing and realisations and on margins.
- Revenue moderation was driven by slower order inflows, lower oil and gas expenditure and pressure on market realisations, while quantity dispatched did not see material change.
- Going forward, improved capacity utilisation, higher value addition and a recovery in oil and gas-related demand are expected to remain important drivers of operating performance.
- Long-term structural demand support from India's growing energy requirements, oil and gas exploration and production, pipeline networks, city gas distribution, water infrastructure and industrial projects.
- Medium and long-term opportunity from import substitution and increasing demand for technically specialised products; ability to develop value-added products, maintain quality and build long-term customer relationships is expected to remain a key differentiator.
- Near-term recovery in the seamless pipe business is expected to remain dependent on the revival of oil and gas expenditure, tendering activity and project awards.
- Key catalysts named for recovery in volumes, realisations and operating profitability: a sustained improvement in oil and gas expenditure and tendering activity, together with moderation in import pressure.
- Margin levers cited: pricing discipline, improved product mix, manufacturing efficiencies and greater contribution from value-added products.
- The strong balance sheet and substantial treasury position are described as a competitive advantage in a cyclical industry, providing flexibility to evaluate strategic opportunities when valuations become attractive.
- Exports are influenced by global trade developments, competitive pricing and evolving tariff and trade arrangements; realignment of global supply chains is seen as an opportunity for India and for MSL.
- Management describes FY 2025-26 as a year of operating moderation rather than financial stress, driven by external and cyclical factors, and remains cautiously optimistic on India's energy and infrastructure structural growth.
- The order book was at its lowest towards the initial part of FY 2025-26 and gradually revived as the year progressed but still remained below the levels anticipated.
- Order booking declined significantly during the first quarter as tendering activity by oil and gas companies remained below expectations.
- The order book subsequently improved and remained at healthy levels through the year, providing reasonable near-term revenue visibility.
- The order book generally provides approximately three to four months of revenue visibility.
- The ability to replenish the order book during a period of subdued industry demand is cited as evidence of the Company's established market position and customer relationships.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA/ton guided at INR 10k-15k. Raw material (HRC) price hikes passed through via back-to-back booking. Safeguard duty on steel not applicable to seamless segment. Margin improvement in Q3 was primarily due to reversal of prior quarter's inventory markdown.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Aggressive cash conservation (INR 3,500 cr liquid investments, ~50% of market cap). Dividend quadrupled FY22-FY24, maintained in FY25 despite lower profits. No buyback or special dividend planned; management prioritizes survival/cyclical resilience over short-term distribution. Treasury portfolio returned >24% in 9M FY26.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company undertakes capital expenditure selectively, favouring projects that enhance manufacturing capabilities, remove operational bottlenecks and improve long-term returns, and funds the programme through internal accruals. The key project completed during FY 2025-26 was the cold-drawn pipes facility. The Company also progressed with the Telangana finishing line project, which is intended primarily to address an existing finishing bottleneck; Management expects it to enable better utilisation of existing production capacity that is currently constrained by the absence of commensurate finishing capacities. No commissioning date is stated for the Telangana finishing line. Alongside physical capex, the Company continued work on new product development and premium connections, with a licensing arrangement with JFE through Jindal Premium Connections giving access to advanced premium connection technology, and is building a fully integrated ERP platform connecting manufacturing, procurement, inventory, sales, logistics and finance. Management states it will continue to evaluate capital expenditure opportunities based on market demand, strategic relevance and expected returns while maintaining a disciplined approach to capital allocation, and will also evaluate selective inorganic opportunities where assets can be acquired at appropriate valuations. Plant-level technology-absorption work during the year covered the 7" Mill, 6" Mill, 14" Mill, OCTG, Coating Plant and the United Seamless Plant, including drive and PLC upgrades, and new sizes rolled at the United Seamless Plant. The Directors' Report also notes that the Board approved on 22 May 2026 a Scheme of Arrangement for demerger of two business undertakings into two subsidiary companies, which is under further review.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Defensive and conservative; Emphasizes survival track record (35 years) over growth at any cost; Dismissive of shareholder pressure to deploy cash; Transparent on one-offs (markdown reversal) but opaque on specific product mix percentages.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Strong balance sheet and substantial treasury position, described by Management as an important competitive advantage in a cyclical industry, enabling working capital and capex to be funded largely through internal resources
- Established customer relationships that allowed the Company to sustain dispatch levels through a year of lower order inflows
- Technical expertise and a diversified product portfolio spanning cold-drawn pipes, cylinder pipes, drill pipes, sour-service subsea seamless pipes and premium connections, addressing import-substitution and higher-value applications
- Licensing arrangement with JFE through Jindal Premium Connections, giving access to advanced premium connection technology
- Pricing discipline: the Company chose to protect profitability rather than pursue volumes through aggressive pricing
- Multi-location manufacturing footprint across Maharashtra and Telangana plus captive wind and solar power assets

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Government capex delay (Oil & Gas dependency); Chinese import dumping (20-25% of domestic market); Demand stagnation without budget stimulus; Execution risk on premium connections launch; CFO turnover history (though current CFO tenure 1.5 years).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The margin beat is largely an accounting artifact (inventory markdown reversal) telegraphed last quarter, not operational leverage. The company sits on massive cash (INR 3,500 cr) earning >24% returns, effectively acting as a hedge fund with a pipe manufacturing attached, yet refuses to return excess capital citing industry bankruptcy risks.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Strengthen the core seamless and specialised pipe business, particularly across the oil and gas and infrastructure sectors.
- Increase the contribution of specialised and value-added products (cold-drawn pipes, cylinder pipes, drill pipes, sour-service subsea seamless pipes, premium connections) to improve differentiation and realisations, and reduce dependence on commodity-oriented volumes.
- Move from being primarily a volume-driven manufacturer to an increasingly technology- and value-added-product-oriented company, using the licensing arrangement with JFE through Jindal Premium Connections …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Order book] Order book as on 31 July 2026 of Rs 1,709 crore — Maharashtra Rs 1,374 crore, Telangana Rs 160 crore, ERW Rs 175 crore; ONGC & OIL account for Rs 714 crore (42%) and Others Rs 995 crore (58%), including drill pipe orders of Rs 2 crore and cylinder pipe orders of Rs 100 crore.
- [Anti-dumping] Anti-dumping duty by way of a minimum import price was implemented for 5 years from 28 October 2021 on various types of seamless pipes from China, and "As an interim measure, this duty has been further extended till 27 January 2027."
- [DMI & SP policy] "Ministry of Steel has revised their DMI & SP policy from 01 April 2025 for 5 years. Seamless & ERW pipes have been made 'Melt & Pour' in the revised policy which means that in all PSU projects, seamless & ERW pipes made only from domestic steel can be supplied." For requirements up to Rs 200 crores, only domestic tenders are floated, excluding foreign players.
- [Demand environment] Tender issuance by oil companies has slowed from earlier levels; per Ind-Ra's 2QFY26 Project Tracker project awards declined 27% yoy in H1 FY26 and 13% yoy in Q2 FY26, with record tender announcements but delayed awarding; crude oil output dropped 2.5% yoy in 2024-25 and natural gas production declined 1%.
- [Market sizing] Company estimate: around 500 new onshore and offshore wells drilled every year at a conservative 200 mt of seamless pipe per well implies "fresh requirement of 100,000 mt per year", in addition to development and work-over wells; ONGC with OPaL and MRPL plan to double production to 8 MMTPA by 2030 spending Rs 1 lakh crore.
- [Shareholding] As on 30 June 2026: Promoters 70.28%, FII 9.72%, DII 3.84%, Others 16.16%; FII holding rose from 9.58% and DII from 3.29% versus Q4 FY26, taking FII+DII from 12.87% to 13.56% across 194 investors, with marquee holders including Quant, Vanguard funds, Abakkus, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, Acadian and ICICI Prudential Energy Opportunities Fund.
